title: Ocean Animal Variety
keyIdea: The ocean is home to a huge variety of animals. They come in every size, from a clownfish about as long as your hand to the blue whale, the biggest animal that has ever lived. They come in many shapes: star-shaped sea stars, long thin eels, flat rays, spiky pufferfish and octopuses with eight arms. Not all of them are fish. A seahorse is a fish, but a sea star, a jellyfish, a crab and a whale are not. Variety means how many different kinds there are.
familyTip: Look at a picture of a rock pool, a reef or a fish counter together. Count the animals, then count the kinds. Ask: which is the biggest? Which shape is strangest? Which ones are fish, and which are not?

visual.caption: Fish or not a fish? Drag each card, or tap it then a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: line ocean animals up by size, match body shapes, sort fish from not fish, match ways of moving and count the kinds on a reef.

kid: The ocean is home to lots of different animals. A clownfish is about as long as your hand. A blue whale is longer than two buses. It is the biggest animal that has ever lived, bigger than any dinosaur.

Sea animals come in many shapes. A sea star is shaped like a star. An eel is long and thin. A stingray is flat, like a pancake. A pufferfish can puff up into a spiky ball. An octopus has eight long arms.
Not every sea animal is a fish. A fish has gills to breathe under water and fins to swim. A seahorse is a fish! But a sea star, a jellyfish, a crab and a whale are not fish.
Sea animals move in different ways too. Fish swim with fins and a tail. Crabs walk sideways on their legs. An octopus squirts out water to shoot along. Turtles flap big flippers.
adult: Ages 5 to 7. This fits the National Curriculum in England, Year 1 science (identify and name a variety of common animals, including fish and mammals, and compare their structure) and Year 2 (living things and their habitats). Key words: variety, kind, fish, mammal, gills, fins, flippers, size, shape.

The blue whale grows to about 30 m and is the largest animal known to have lived. An adult great white shark is about 4 to 5 m, a green sea turtle shell about 1 m, and a clownfish about 10 cm. Seahorses are true fish, with gills, fins and a swim bladder. Sea stars and jellyfish are invertebrates without backbones. Crabs are crustaceans. Whales and dolphins are mammals.

Common mistakes: thinking every sea animal is a fish (so sea stars and jellyfish get called fish); thinking a seahorse is not a fish because of its name and shape; thinking a dinosaur or a shark was the biggest animal ever; and counting animals when asked for kinds. Three clownfish and one crab are four animals but only two kinds.

In the lab your child drags four animals onto a size line from smallest to biggest, matches five animals to body shapes, sorts seven into fish and not a fish, and matches four to how they move. Last, they tap every different kind on a reef: nine animals, but six kinds. Every action also has a button.

practice.prompt: Which is the biggest animal that has ever lived?
practice.hint: It lives in the ocean and is longer than two buses.
practice.explain: The blue whale is the biggest animal ever. It is bigger than any dinosaur and much bigger than a shark.

choices: yes, it has gills and fins
no, it is a kind of horse
practice.hint: Think about how a seahorse breathes under water.
practice.explain: A seahorse is a fish. It breathes with gills and swims with small fins.

practice.prompt: A rock pool has {a} crabs and {b} shrimps. How many animals is that?
practice.hint: Put the two groups together: {a} and {b} more.
practice.explain: {a} + {b} = {=a+b} animals, but only 2 kinds: crabs and shrimps.

practice.prompt: A crab has 2 big claws. How many claws do {n} crabs have?
practice.hint: Count in twos, once for each crab.
practice.explain: {n} × 2 = {=2*n}. Each crab has 2 claws, so {n} crabs have {=2*n} claws.

practice.prompt: Which animal is NOT a fish?
practice.hint: A fish has fins and gills. Which one has neither?
practice.explain: A jellyfish is not a fish. It has no bones, no fins and no gills. Clownfish and sharks are fish.

pool.prompt: Is a sea star (starfish) a fish?
choices: no, it has no fins and no gills like a fish
yes, because it is called starfish
yes, every sea animal is a fish
pool.hint: Look past the name. Does it have fins?
pool.explain: A sea star is not a fish, even though some people call it a starfish.

choices: long and thin, like a rope
pool.hint: A stingray glides along the sea floor.
pool.explain: A stingray is flat. An eel is long and thin, and a puffed-up pufferfish is round and spiky.

choices: it walks sideways on its legs
it squirts out a jet of water
pool.hint: Look at the crab's legs and how it walks along the sand.
pool.explain: Crabs walk, often sideways, on their legs. An octopus uses a water jet, and a turtle flaps flippers.

pool.prompt: Which ocean animal is about as long as your hand?
pool.hint: Think small: which one could sit on your open hand?
pool.explain: A clownfish is small, about as long as your hand. Whales and sharks are much bigger.

pool.prompt: A reef has {a} clownfish and {b} turtles. How many kinds of animal is that?
pool.hint: Count kinds, not animals. How many different animals are there?
pool.explain: There are {=a+b} animals, but only 2 kinds: clownfish and turtles.

pool.prompt: Why is a whale not a fish?
choices: it breathes air and feeds its baby milk
it is too big to be a fish
pool.explain: A whale breathes air and feeds its baby milk, so it is a mammal, not a fish.

pool.prompt: Which animal has eight long arms?
pool.hint: It can squirt water to shoot along.
pool.explain: An octopus has eight arms. A sea star usually has five, and an eel has none.

pool.prompt: A diver sees {n} sea stars. Each has 5 arms. How many arms is that?
pool.hint: Count on in fives, once for each sea star.
pool.explain: {n} × 5 = {=5*n} arms. Most sea stars have 5 arms each.
